fixes.explanation: That's what the scribes say. Jesus opens with, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?” (Mark 12:35). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and the scribes tie the Christ to his family. Hold on to that answer, friend, because Jesus is about to do something with it.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a giant in the Bible, so I get why he came to mind. But the text says the scribes call the Christ the Son of David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). Right kind of big name, just a different family.

Aaron was Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and he's a big name too. But the scribes in this passage say the Christ is the Son of David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). I once spent years in a junk drawer and lost track of plenty of names, so I understand a mix-up. Mark 12:35 keeps it simple, though.

That's the one. David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), is speaking by the Holy Spirit, and the words are “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.” (Mark 12:36). A seat at the right hand, friend.

No packing needed on this one. Nothing in David's words sends anyone to Egypt. David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), speaks of the Lord telling his Lord to sit until the enemies are put under His feet (Mark 12:36). It's a seat, not a road trip.

Building a house does come up in David's own story, when God says David's offspring will build a house for His Name (2 Samuel 7:13). But that's not what's in the words Jesus quotes here. In Mark 12:36, the Lord's word to David's Lord is “Sit at My right hand…”
Not quite, friend. The text says “…the large crowd listened to Him with delight.” (Mark 12:37). Delight is a long way from upset.

That's right. The scribes want the chief seats in the synagogues and “…the places of honor at banquets.” (Mark 12:39). They want the best spot in the room. I spent years in a junk drawer, so I'd settle for any spot that isn't under a takeout menu.

A silver shekel would be a nice upgrade, but it's not what she brings. Mark 12:42 says she put in two small copper coins, which amounted to a small fraction of a denarius. Not a shekel in sight, friend.

Yes, and Jesus says it plainly: “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.” That includes the many rich people who put in large amounts (Mark 12:41). He calls His disciples to Him to say it.
